neurips-2008-from-online-to-batch-learni.problem: Online learners update their model one example at a time, but many applications need one final model trained on a fixed dataset. Standard conversion methods do not suit every online learner.
neurips-2008-from-online-to-batch-learni.idea: Cutoff averaging combines a selected portion of the learner's successive models. It adapts this conversion to the behavior of conservative online algorithms while retaining their computational efficiency.
neurips-2008-from-online-to-batch-learni.results: The paper provides a statistical analysis and experiments supporting the conversion method, positioning it for datasets where efficient training matters.
neurips-2008-from-online-to-batch-learni.limitations: The abstract restricts the method to conservative online algorithms and gives neither experimental datasets nor numerical comparisons, so its practical advantage cannot be quantified here.
neurips-2008-from-online-to-batch-learni.tldr: Adaptively average an online learner's models to obtain an efficient batch predictor.

neurips-2009-an-integer-projected-fixed-.problem: Matching features between images and finding the most likely joint labeling both require discrete choices. Solving an easier continuous problem and rounding afterward can lose solution quality.
neurips-2009-an-integer-projected-fixed-.idea: The proposed fixed point algorithm explicitly seeks discrete assignments while improving a quadratic score. It can run independently or refine another graph matching method's output.
neurips-2009-an-integer-projected-fixed-.results: Experiments report improvements over existing matching methods and over ICM and max-product belief propagation for inference. The algorithm also has score-improvement and convergence properties.
neurips-2009-an-integer-projected-fixed-.limitations: These properties do not establish that the global optimum is found for an NP-hard problem. The abstract provides no dataset-level scores or runtime measurements.
neurips-2009-an-integer-projected-fixed-.tldr: Treat the discrete assignment step as a central part of optimization instead of a final rounding operation.

neurips-2009-the-wisdom-of-crowds-in-the.problem: People remembering historical sequences or rankings make different mistakes. The challenge is to combine their recollections into an ordering closer to the truth.
neurips-2009-the-wisdom-of-crowds-in-the.idea: Two Bayesian models describe a person's answer as either a noisy version of an unknown true ordering or a guess. Sampling-based inference jointly estimates the ordering and participants' strategies.
neurips-2009-the-wisdom-of-crowds-in-the.results: Across the reported general knowledge tasks, aggregated rankings were closer to the correct order than the ranking supplied by even the best individual.
neurips-2009-the-wisdom-of-crowds-in-the.limitations: The findings concern the studied ordering tasks and rely on particular models of memory errors and guessing. The abstract does not describe participant counts or the size of the improvements.
neurips-2009-the-wisdom-of-crowds-in-the.tldr: Modeling how people misremember rankings can make a group's combined recollection more accurate than any individual's.

neurips-2010-learning-efficient-markov-n.problem: Probabilistic networks with many connections usually make inference expensive. Restricting network structure can restore efficiency but exclude useful patterns of dependence.
neurips-2010-learning-efficient-markov-n.idea: The learner finds conditions that split variables into independent groups, then recursively models those simpler pieces. This exploits independence that appears only in particular contexts, alongside deterministic relationships.
neurips-2010-learning-efficient-markov-n.results: The resulting model class supports polynomial-time inference and closed-form weight learning. Experiments compare favorably with several structure learners; the paper also provides probabilistic guarantees under stated assumptions.
neurips-2010-learning-efficient-markov-n.limitations: The guarantees require bounded feature length and bounded dependence strength. A faster greedy version gives up those guarantees, creating a practical tradeoff between speed and theoretical assurance.
neurips-2010-learning-efficient-markov-n.tldr: Complex-looking networks can remain computationally manageable when their conditional structure breaks into simpler pieces.

neurips-2011-inferring-interaction-netwo.problem: Biological interaction measurements are noisy, and researchers also want to discover groups of entities with related behavior. These two goals can inform each other.
neurips-2011-inferring-interaction-netwo.idea: The method extends the Indian Buffet Process, a Bayesian model allowing flexible latent features, to combine interaction scores with attributes of individual entities. It infers both links and node groupings.
neurips-2011-inferring-interaction-netwo.results: Tests on synthetic and real data report better performance than prior methods, recovery of interactions and clusters, and useful predictions about microRNA regulation of mRNA.
neurips-2011-inferring-interaction-netwo.limitations: The abstract gives no accuracy numbers or details about biological validation. Evidence from the described application does not establish equal performance across other biological or social networks.
neurips-2011-inferring-interaction-netwo.tldr: Learn network connections and hidden groups together by combining noisy pairwise evidence with information about each entity.

neurips-2012-factorial-lda-sparse-multi-.problem: Documents vary along several overlapping dimensions, such as subject, viewpoint, and sentiment. A single topic label can blur these distinct influences on word choice.
neurips-2012-factorial-lda-sparse-multi-.idea: Factorial LDA gives each document several latent factors and lets every word depend on a combination of their values. Structured word priors and sparsity help organize those combinations.
neurips-2012-factorial-lda-sparse-multi-.results: On research abstracts, the model discovers factors corresponding to topic, discipline, and methodological versus application focus. The reported changes improve predictive perplexity and human interpretability.
neurips-2012-factorial-lda-sparse-multi-.limitations: The abstract describes one kind of text collection and does not specify the magnitude of the improvements or how interpretability was measured. The meaning of learned factors still requires interpretation.
neurips-2012-factorial-lda-sparse-multi-.tldr: Explain text through several interacting hidden dimensions rather than one undifferentiated collection of topics.

neurips-2012-imagenet-classification-wit.problem: Recognizing objects across a large image collection requires learning features that distinguish many categories despite substantial visual variation. Earlier systems left considerable classification error.
neurips-2012-imagenet-classification-wit.idea: The authors train a large convolutional network using efficient GPU computation, non-saturating neurons, and a regularization method to reduce overfitting in its fully connected layers.
neurips-2012-imagenet-classification-wit.results: Training uses 1.3 million ImageNet images across 1,000 classes. Reported test errors are 39.7% for the top prediction and 18.9% when any of the five highest-ranked predictions counts as correct.
neurips-2012-imagenet-classification-wit.limitations: The evidence concerns the stated ImageNet task. The abstract does not establish performance under distribution shifts or specify the computational cost of training the 60-million-parameter model.
neurips-2012-imagenet-classification-wit.tldr: A large, efficiently trained convolutional network substantially improves the reported ImageNet classification results.

neurips-2012-online-l1-dictionary-learni.problem: Finding genuinely new information in a fast document stream requires updating a model without repeatedly retraining on all previous text. Batch dictionary learning can be too slow.
neurips-2012-online-l1-dictionary-learni.idea: The algorithm incrementally learns reusable document components and measures reconstruction error with absolute differences. An alternating-directions optimization method makes these updates efficient.
neurips-2012-online-l1-dictionary-learni.results: The paper proves sublinear regret and reports more than a tenfold speedup over a previous batch method on news and Twitter data, without significant loss of detection quality.
neurips-2012-online-l1-dictionary-learni.limitations: The abstract does not detail novelty labels, evaluation measures, or how performance changes with different stream characteristics. The regret guarantee and empirical detection quality address different aspects of the method.
neurips-2012-online-l1-dictionary-learni.tldr: Update a text dictionary online to detect novel documents much faster than the compared batch approach.

neurips-2012-reducing-statistical-time-s.problem: Many statistical questions about time series involve strongly dependent observations, while familiar classifiers are usually introduced for independent examples. This seems to limit reuse of classification tools.
neurips-2012-reducing-statistical-time-s.idea: The paper constructs a distance between time-series distributions that can be evaluated through binary classification. That distance becomes a building block for clustering and several distribution-comparison problems.
neurips-2012-reducing-statistical-time-s.results: The authors prove universal consistency under their general assumptions and illustrate the theory using synthetic and real-world data.
neurips-2012-reducing-statistical-time-s.limitations: The abstract does not spell out the assumptions, convergence rates, or practical sample requirements. An eventual consistency guarantee alone does not tell users how reliable a decision is for a short observed series.
neurips-2012-reducing-statistical-time-s.tldr: Turn comparisons between dependent time series into classification problems through a suitable distributional distance.

neurips-2013-neural-representation-of-ac.problem: Some brain responses distinguish an action despite changes in its actor, while others distinguish the actor across actions. Explaining these individual-neuron responses from visual input remains challenging.
neurips-2013-neural-representation-of-ac.idea: A simple model combines responses to short action fragments from visual pathways associated with form and motion. Different linear weights produce different kinds of selectivity.
neurips-2013-neural-representation-of-ac.results: The model fits the recorded neural responses surprisingly well. Even a single input pathway can support actor-invariant or action-invariant responses through different weighting patterns.
neurips-2013-neural-representation-of-ac.limitations: A successful fit does not by itself establish the brain's causal mechanism. The abstract does not report dataset size, quantitative fit quality, or performance beyond the measured action stimuli.
neurips-2013-neural-representation-of-ac.tldr: Simple weighted combinations of short visual action fragments can explain several observed forms of neural invariance.

neurips-2013-regret-based-robust-solutio.problem: Decision makers may be uncertain about both rewards and how actions change the world. Optimizing only the worst possible outcome can be an overly narrow robustness objective.
neurips-2013-regret-based-robust-solutio.idea: The paper instead minimizes worst-case regret: the loss relative to the best policy for whichever model is realized. Sampling methods accommodate dependent uncertainty in rewards and transitions across decisions.
neurips-2013-regret-based-robust-solutio.results: The authors provide quality bounds, comparisons with benchmark algorithms on two established domains, and an analysis that estimates error bounds after sampling.
neurips-2013-regret-based-robust-solutio.limitations: The abstract does not quantify empirical gains or the samples needed for useful bounds. Its demonstrations cover two domains, and the guarantees depend on the sampling and uncertainty formulation.
neurips-2013-regret-based-robust-solutio.tldr: Choose robust policies by limiting missed opportunities across uncertain models of rewards and transitions.

neurips-2013-universal-models-for-binary.problem: Neural population recordings contain complex patterns of simultaneous firing. Models built from only simple interactions may miss structure, while more expressive alternatives can become computationally impractical.
neurips-2013-universal-models-for-binary.idea: A Dirichlet-process model combines a compact parametric starting distribution with the flexibility of a histogram. This permits arbitrary binary spike-pattern distributions while borrowing structure from the starting model.
neurips-2013-universal-models-for-binary.results: The paper develops efficient inference for two base distributions, connects one to the pairwise Ising model under a stated condition, and demonstrates the models on neural recordings.
neurips-2013-universal-models-for-binary.limitations: Universal representational ability does not guarantee accurate estimation from limited recordings. The abstract gives no population sizes, numerical comparisons, or details of the equivalence condition.
neurips-2013-universal-models-for-binary.tldr: Combine a structured baseline with flexible Bayesian corrections to model complex patterns of neurons firing together.

neurips-2013-variational-inference-for-m.problem: Gaussian process regression depends on settings controlling which inputs count as similar. Choosing a single best setting can ignore uncertainty, especially when inputs have many dimensions.
neurips-2013-variational-inference-for-m.idea: The method approximately averages over kernel hyperparameters using variational inference, a tractable approximation to Bayesian reasoning. A standardized representation of the Gaussian process supports learning flexible Mahalanobis distance metrics.
neurips-2013-variational-inference-for-m.results: The authors evaluate the approach on datasets with high-dimensional inputs and compare it with existing methods for this regression setting.
neurips-2013-variational-inference-for-m.limitations: The abstract does not state whether the method outperforms the comparisons, by how much, or at what computational cost. Approximate integration also leaves an unquantified gap from exact Bayesian averaging.
neurips-2013-variational-inference-for-m.tldr: Account for uncertainty in a Gaussian process's similarity rule instead of fixing every kernel setting to one estimate.

neurips-2014-generative-adversarial-nets.problem: A generative model must learn to produce samples resembling real data. The challenge is to train such a model without relying on costly sampling chains or elaborate inference machinery.
neurips-2014-generative-adversarial-nets.idea: Two networks compete: a generator creates samples, and a discriminator tries to distinguish them from training examples. The generator learns by making the discriminator's task harder.
neurips-2014-generative-adversarial-nets.results: For unrestricted functions, the game has an ideal solution that reproduces the data distribution. Neural-network versions train with backpropagation, and experiments provide qualitative and quantitative demonstrations.
neurips-2014-generative-adversarial-nets.limitations: The ideal theoretical solution assumes unrestricted functions; it does not establish that practical neural-network training reaches that solution. The abstract gives no detailed experimental scores.
neurips-2014-generative-adversarial-nets.tldr: Teach a generator to imitate data by training it against a learned detector of generated samples.

neurips-2014-optimization-methods-for-sp.problem: Learning a sparse graph of conditional relationships in high-dimensional data needs scalable optimization. Existing fast methods often depend on Gaussian distribution assumptions.
neurips-2014-optimization-methods-for-sp.idea: The paper applies two proximal-gradient methods to CONCORD, a convex pseudo-likelihood framework. These methods combine gradient steps with operations encouraging many estimated connections to become zero.
neurips-2014-optimization-methods-for-sp.results: The authors prove convergence and convergence rates. Timing comparisons with coordinate-wise minimization report substantial speed and scalability improvements for the studied graph-estimation problems outside the Gaussian setting.
neurips-2014-optimization-methods-for-sp.limitations: The abstract supplies no numerical timings or detailed data conditions. Faster optimization of this objective does not itself demonstrate accurate graph recovery for every non-Gaussian distribution.
neurips-2014-optimization-methods-for-sp.tldr: Use modern sparse optimization methods to accelerate a graph-learning objective that extends beyond the Gaussian framework.

neurips-2014-projective-dictionary-pair-.problem: Dictionary-based classifiers represent an input through learned components, but enforcing sparse representations can make both training and prediction expensive. This limits otherwise useful visual recognition methods.
neurips-2014-projective-dictionary-pair-.idea: Projective dictionary pair learning jointly trains two dictionaries: one projects inputs into a representation, and the other reconstructs them. The pair is trained to preserve useful signal information and separate classes.
neurips-2014-projective-dictionary-pair-.results: The abstract reports greatly reduced training and testing complexity alongside competitive accuracy across several visual classification tasks.
neurips-2014-projective-dictionary-pair-.limitations: No numerical runtime or accuracy comparisons are included in the abstract. It also does not identify the tested tasks, so the size and breadth of the practical advantage remain unclear.
neurips-2014-projective-dictionary-pair-.tldr: Learn a direct projection and a reconstruction dictionary together to make dictionary-based classification faster.

neurips-2015-gradient-free-hamiltonian-m.problem: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo explores probability distributions efficiently by using gradients, but some target distributions have gradients that are unavailable or too costly to calculate.
neurips-2015-gradient-free-hamiltonian-m.idea: Kernel Hamiltonian Monte Carlo learns an approximate gradient field from samples using a flexible kernel-based density model. Two approximations reduce the cost of using that learned field.
neurips-2015-gradient-free-hamiltonian-m.results: The method is asymptotically exact and reportedly mixes better than leading gradient-free alternatives. Experiments include toy problems, real applications, approximate Bayesian computation, and exact-approximate sampling.
neurips-2015-gradient-free-hamiltonian-m.limitations: Asymptotic correctness concerns long-run behavior, not the accuracy of a finite sampling run. The abstract does not quantify training overhead, mixing gains, or the number of samples needed to learn useful gradients.
neurips-2015-gradient-free-hamiltonian-m.tldr: Learn the gradients needed for efficient sampling when direct gradients of the target distribution are unavailable.

neurips-2015-weakly-supervised-disentang.problem: A single photograph hides much of an object's three-dimensional structure, making it difficult to predict how that object would look from another angle.
neurips-2015-weakly-supervised-disentang.idea: A recurrent convolutional encoder-decoder learns to apply sequences of rotations. Its internal representation can separate aspects of an object while preserving information across a sequence of generated views.
neurips-2015-weakly-supervised-disentang.results: The authors demonstrate predicted views for faces in Multi-PIE and for three-dimensional chair models. They also show separation of latent factors without using object-class labels.
neurips-2015-weakly-supervised-disentang.limitations: The approach relies on ample training data for specific object classes. The abstract does not establish generalization to arbitrary objects or quantify the accuracy of geometry hidden in the input image.
neurips-2015-weakly-supervised-disentang.tldr: Learn repeated view transformations from examples to rotate faces and chairs starting with one image.

neurips-2016-bayesian-optimization-with-.problem: When evaluating a function is expensive, an optimizer must choose carefully where to spend a fixed number of evaluations. A locally appealing choice may waste later opportunities.
neurips-2016-bayesian-optimization-with-.idea: The paper expresses budget-aware Bayesian optimization as a sequential planning problem. Rollout approximations estimate the consequences of candidate actions using tailored future-search heuristics.
neurips-2016-bayesian-optimization-with-.results: Numerical experiments report that the resulting finite-budget optimizer outperforms several popular Bayesian optimization methods.
neurips-2016-bayesian-optimization-with-.limitations: The exact planning problem has a continuously expanding state space, so the proposed strategy remains approximate. The abstract gives no benchmark details, improvement sizes, or planning overhead, all of which matter when deciding whether lookahead is worthwhile.
neurips-2016-bayesian-optimization-with-.tldr: Plan how to use the remaining evaluation budget instead of choosing each expensive experiment in isolation.

neurips-2016-learning-sensor-multiplexin.problem: A color sensor usually measures only one color at each pixel, leaving software to reconstruct the others. Designing the sensor pattern separately from reconstruction can miss useful combinations.
neurips-2016-learning-sensor-multiplexin.idea: The method represents the choice of color measured at each location as a learnable layer. Backpropagation jointly adjusts this sensor pattern and the neural network reconstructing a full-color image.
neurips-2016-learning-sensor-multiplexin.results: The learned design improves reconstruction accuracy over the Bayer pattern and refines a sparse measurement layout resembling a recent alternative design.
neurips-2016-learning-sensor-multiplexin.limitations: The abstract does not quantify accuracy gains or describe deployment in manufactured camera hardware. Its design choices are limited to selecting channels from a fixed set.
neurips-2016-learning-sensor-multiplexin.tldr: Optimize the camera's color sampling pattern and its reconstruction software as one end-to-end system.

neurips-2016-solving-marginal-map-proble.problem: Some probabilistic decisions require maximizing over choices while summing over uncertain hidden outcomes. This combination, called marginal MAP, can be harder than either operation alone.
neurips-2016-solving-marginal-map-proble.idea: XOR MMAP replaces the difficult counting component with constrained queries to optimization or satisfiability-style oracles. Added parity constraints support a compact reformulation of the overall problem.
neurips-2016-solving-marginal-map-proble.results: The paper establishes a constant-factor approximation through an optimization encoding of polynomial size. Evaluations in several decision-making and machine-learning applications outperform multiple existing marginal MAP solvers.
neurips-2016-solving-marginal-map-proble.limitations: A polynomial-size encoding does not imply that its oracle calls are easy to solve. The abstract does not state the approximation constant, runtime figures, or application-specific performance.
neurips-2016-solving-marginal-map-proble.tldr: Use parity-constrained oracle queries to approximate decisions that combine optimization with probabilistic counting.

neurips-2017-adaptive-stimulus-selection.problem: Choosing a stimulus that strongly activates one neuron need not reveal diverse responses across a whole population. Experiments therefore need objectives that reflect many recorded neurons together.
neurips-2017-adaptive-stimulus-selection.idea: Adept adaptively selects images using population-level objectives and predictions built from deep-network image features. Neural measurements feed back into subsequent stimulus selection.
neurips-2017-adaptive-stimulus-selection.results: Simulations show more varied responses from population objectives. In macaque V4 recordings, selected images produced mean responses 20% larger than randomly selected natural images and greater response diversity.
neurips-2017-adaptive-stimulus-selection.limitations: The live experimental evidence described concerns macaque V4 and the studied image setting. The abstract does not establish equivalent benefits for other brain regions or stimulus modalities.
neurips-2017-adaptive-stimulus-selection.tldr: Select visual stimuli adaptively to probe an entire neural population more effectively.

neurips-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-3.problem: Sequence-to-sequence systems such as translation models need to connect information across an input sentence. Recurrent and convolutional architectures can complicate training and limit parallel computation.
neurips-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-3.idea: The proposed architecture uses attention alone, allowing positions in a sequence to draw directly on relevant information elsewhere. It removes recurrence and convolution from the encoder-decoder design.
neurips-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-3.results: On two translation tasks, the models improve quality while training faster and supporting greater parallelism. The abstract reports 27.5 BLEU for English-to-German and 41.1 for English-to-French.
neurips-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-3.limitations: These results concern the reported translation benchmarks. The abstract does not establish performance on other sequence tasks or describe how computational costs scale with increasingly long sequences.
neurips-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-3.tldr: Build a translation network around attention to improve both prediction quality and parallel training.

neurips-2018-empirical-risk-minimization.problem: Private learning is difficult when each person must hide their own data before communicating with a server, and the server cannot ask follow-up questions. Dimensionality can make accuracy costly.
neurips-2018-empirical-risk-minimization.idea: For smooth losses, polynomial approximations improve sample requirements. The paper also develops one-bit user messages with constant per-user computation and uses geometric properties of constrained models for high-dimensional cases.
neurips-2018-empirical-risk-minimization.results: Theoretical bounds improve previous dimensional dependence under the stated conditions. User-efficient variants preserve asymptotic error bounds, while additional assumptions enable efficient server computation.
neurips-2018-empirical-risk-minimization.limitations: The improvements rely on smoothness, loss structure, or further server-side assumptions. The abstract does not provide empirical privacy-accuracy measurements or remove all computational constraints in every setting.
neurips-2018-empirical-risk-minimization.tldr: Exploit smoothness and model geometry to make non-interactive locally private learning more efficient.

neurips-2018-learning-from-discriminativ.problem: A label tells a classifier that it made a mistake but may not explain why. Simple distinguishing features could make each correction more informative.
neurips-2018-learning-from-discriminativ.idea: The learning interaction supplies both the correct class and a discriminative feature explaining a relevant distinction. An online algorithm uses this feedback for target concepts represented by decision trees or a specified logical subclass.
neurips-2018-learning-from-discriminativ.results: The paper proves tight mistake bounds depending on target-concept size rather than the total number of possible features, which may even be infinite. It also includes an experimental demonstration.
neurips-2018-learning-from-discriminativ.limitations: The guarantees assume appropriate discriminative feedback and a restricted target-concept family. The abstract does not explain how robust the method is to inconsistent or mistaken human explanations.
neurips-2018-learning-from-discriminativ.tldr: Teach a classifier with short feature-based explanations so learning depends on concept complexity, not feature-space size.

neurips-2018-predictive-uncertainty-esti.problem: An uncertain prediction can arise because an example is ambiguous or because it is unlike the training data. Those situations may require different responses from a deployed classifier.
neurips-2018-predictive-uncertainty-esti.idea: Prior Networks predict a distribution over possible predictive distributions. This extra layer explicitly represents uncertainty caused by a mismatch between training and test data.
neurips-2018-predictive-uncertainty-esti.results: On MNIST and CIFAR-10, the approach outperforms previous methods for out-of-distribution detection and misclassification detection. Synthetic and image experiments also demonstrate separation of data ambiguity from distributional uncertainty.
neurips-2018-predictive-uncertainty-esti.limitations: The evidence covers the reported datasets and evaluations. The abstract does not establish reliable detection of every unfamiliar distribution or provide numerical gains and calibration results.
neurips-2018-predictive-uncertainty-esti.tldr: Represent uncertainty about class probabilities to distinguish ambiguous inputs from inputs outside the training distribution.

neurips-2018-unsupervised-depth-estimati.problem: Rotating or reshaping a face from one image requires depth information that the image does not directly reveal. Collecting ground-truth facial depth for training can be difficult.
neurips-2018-unsupervised-depth-estimati.idea: DepthNets infer depths at facial keypoints and use them inside a differentiable transformation loss. The inferred three-dimensional points are mapped to target two-dimensional facial geometry without ground-truth depth supervision.
neurips-2018-unsupervised-depth-estimati.results: The approach produces plausible pose changes, frontalizations, and three-dimensional face models. The authors also explore adversarial post-processing to regenerate complete head images after transformations.
neurips-2018-unsupervised-depth-estimati.limitations: The authors explicitly identify shortcomings in the formulation, though the abstract does not specify them. Plausible transformations do not establish accurate physical depth, and quantitative reconstruction results are absent.
neurips-2018-unsupervised-depth-estimati.tldr: Learn useful facial depth indirectly through the task of transforming keypoints between poses.

neurips-2019-a-stochastic-composite-grad.problem: Some learning objectives apply one function to an average or finite sum produced by another function. Estimating gradients through this composition introduces additional noise and bias.
neurips-2019-a-stochastic-composite-grad.idea: The proposed stochastic method incrementally reduces variance in estimates of both the inner mapping and its derivative. These coordinated estimates support efficient updates of the composite objective.
neurips-2019-a-stochastic-composite-grad.results: The analysis achieves the same orders of complexity as leading first-order methods for corresponding nonconvex objectives without the extra outer composition.
neurips-2019-a-stochastic-composite-grad.limitations: The result applies to smooth mappings in the specified expectation or finite-sum setting. The abstract does not report experiments, concrete runtime gains, or guarantees of reaching a global optimum in nonconvex problems.
neurips-2019-a-stochastic-composite-grad.tldr: Control noise in both parts of a composite gradient to retain strong stochastic-optimization complexity bounds.

neurips-2019-learning-based-low-rank-app.problem: Low-rank matrix approximation compresses data while preserving important structure. Fast randomized methods first sketch a matrix, but a generic random sketch may ignore recurring patterns in an application's data.
neurips-2019-learning-based-low-rank-app.idea: The authors learn a sparse sketching matrix from training matrices, then use it in the usual low-rank approximation pipeline. Hybrid sketches retain some random rows alongside learned ones.
neurips-2019-learning-based-low-rank-app.results: Experiments report reduced approximation error, sometimes by an order of magnitude. Hybrid sketches preserve worst-case guarantees, and the paper provides generalization bounds and a special-case theoretical analysis.
neurips-2019-learning-based-low-rank-app.limitations: Training requires representative matrices, and the abstract does not quantify training cost. Its strongest empirical improvements are not claimed for every dataset or sketch configuration.
neurips-2019-learning-based-low-rank-app.tldr: Learn how to compress matrices from examples while retaining randomness where worst-case protection is needed.

neurips-2019-mining-gold-samples-for-con.problem: Conditional image generators may represent some parts of the target distribution better than others. Improving them requires a way to identify where generated and real data differ.
neurips-2019-mining-gold-samples-for-con.idea: GOLD estimates a gap between data and model log-densities using the discriminator. That diagnostic guides training-example weights, acceptance of generated samples, and selection of new labeled data.
neurips-2019-mining-gold-samples-for-con.results: Across different image datasets, the proposed methods outperform corresponding baselines in training improvement, rejection sampling, and active learning.
neurips-2019-mining-gold-samples-for-con.limitations: The abstract does not provide the size of the gains, dataset details, or the accuracy of the density-gap estimates. The evidence therefore supports the evaluated applications without establishing universal improvements for conditional generators.
neurips-2019-mining-gold-samples-for-con.tldr: Use a discriminator-derived distribution-gap score to improve what a conditional GAN learns, generates, and requests for labeling.

neurips-2019-mixtape-breaking-the-softma.problem: A standard softmax output layer limits the distributions a language model can express. Mixtures of softmax layers loosen that restriction but consume substantially more time and memory.
neurips-2019-mixtape-breaking-the-softma.idea: Mixtape uses gating in logit space, a tree decomposition based on sigmoid functions, and shared gates to build a more efficient expressive output layer.
neurips-2019-mixtape-breaking-the-softma.results: Across four language-modeling and translation benchmarks, it is 3.5 to 10.5 times more efficient than mixture-of-softmax layers with similar performance. It also improves on standard softmax while adding 20% to 34% runtime for the stated vocabulary sizes.
neurips-2019-mixtape-breaking-the-softma.limitations: The reported overhead concerns vocabularies of 10,000 to 30,000 words. The abstract does not separately detail memory savings or behavior at much larger vocabularies.
neurips-2019-mixtape-breaking-the-softma.tldr: Make a language model's output distribution more expressive without paying the full cost of softmax mixtures.

neurips-2019-modelling-heterogeneous-dis.problem: Regression outputs can have asymmetric, multimodal, or otherwise irregular distributions. Assuming a simple symmetric shape can hide important uncertainty about possible outcomes.
neurips-2019-modelling-heterogeneous-dis.idea: UMAL learns a continuous mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions using a fixed-size neural model. Its connection to quantile regression helps describe different parts of the output distribution.
neurips-2019-modelling-heterogeneous-dis.results: The authors demonstrate the framework on synthetic data, room-price forecasting, and financial activity in personal bank accounts, obtaining valid probability distributions that expose richer outcome information.
neurips-2019-modelling-heterogeneous-dis.limitations: The abstract does not give comparative accuracy, calibration, or runtime measurements. A flexible distributional family alone does not establish that its uncertainty estimates will be reliable for every dataset.
neurips-2019-modelling-heterogeneous-dis.tldr: Predict a flexible distribution of outcomes rather than forcing regression uncertainty into a simple fixed shape.

neurips-2019-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.problem: Stochastic proximal-gradient methods are widely used with regularizers that encourage desirable solutions. Existing finite-iteration analyses did not cover regularizers that are both nonsmooth and nonconvex.
neurips-2019-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.idea: The paper analyzes mini-batch variants for a smooth nonconvex loss combined with such a regularizer. It also develops versions that change batch size without requiring a target accuracy in advance.
neurips-2019-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.results: The resulting complexity bounds match analogous convex-regularizer methods for finding approximate stationary points. Experiments support the effectiveness of the studied approaches against other stochastic methods.
neurips-2019-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.limitations: Stationarity is weaker than global optimality in these nonconvex problems. The abstract does not specify numerical gains or all technical assumptions needed for the bounds.
neurips-2019-non-asymptotic-analysis-of-.tldr: Extend finite-time guarantees for practical stochastic optimization to a broader class of nonconvex regularizers.

neurips-2019-reverse-kl-divergence-train.problem: Prior Networks express uncertainty through distributions over class probabilities, but their original training criterion becomes difficult to use on complex tasks with many classes.
neurips-2019-reverse-kl-divergence-train.idea: The paper changes training to reverse KL divergence between Dirichlet distributions and introduces a generalized adversarial training procedure. This reshapes how target uncertainty distributions are matched.
neurips-2019-reverse-kl-divergence-train.results: The new criterion improves out-of-distribution detection and supports many-class training. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, adaptive attacks that both alter predictions and evade detection require more computation than against the compared defenses.
neurips-2019-reverse-kl-divergence-train.limitations: Greater attack effort is not proof of immunity to adversarial inputs. The abstract does not quantify attack budgets or establish robustness beyond the evaluated attacks and datasets.
neurips-2019-reverse-kl-divergence-train.tldr: Improve Prior Network training so uncertainty estimates scale better and evaluated attacks become harder to hide.

neurips-2019-submodular-function-minimiz.problem: Optimizing a submodular set function becomes harder when every evaluation includes random measurement error. Researchers need to know how solution accuracy improves with more queries.
neurips-2019-submodular-function-minimiz.idea: The paper develops minimization algorithms for zero-mean noisy evaluations and separately studies feedback that returns several function values per query. Lower bounds identify unavoidable error.
neurips-2019-submodular-function-minimiz.results: For ordinary feedback, expected error scales as n to the three-halves divided by the square root of query count. With suitable multi-point feedback, upper and lower bounds match up to constants.
neurips-2019-submodular-function-minimiz.limitations: The optimal multi-point guarantee requires each noisy oracle itself to be submodular and a bounded number of feedback points. The abstract offers theoretical results rather than empirical performance evidence.
neurips-2019-submodular-function-minimiz.tldr: Characterize how noisy function queries limit submodular minimization and when richer feedback achieves optimal accuracy.

neurips-2020-expandnets-linear-over-para.problem: Small convolutional networks are attractive for deployment, but training them directly can be harder than training larger models. The goal is to improve learning without enlarging the final network.
neurips-2020-expandnets-linear-over-para.idea: ExpandNets replace a linear layer with several consecutive linear layers during training, adding no intervening nonlinearity. These layers can then be multiplied together to recover the compact architecture exactly.
neurips-2020-expandnets-linear-over-para.results: Experiments on classification, detection, and segmentation outperform training the compact model from scratch and the compared knowledge-distillation approach. They also report reduced gradient confusion and better generalization.
neurips-2020-expandnets-linear-over-para.limitations: The abstract does not quantify added training cost or give task-specific improvements. Benefits are empirical for the evaluated expansion strategies and networks.
neurips-2020-expandnets-linear-over-para.tldr: Train an expanded linear parameterization, then algebraically fold it back into the original compact network.

neurips-2020-learning-from-failure-de-bi.problem: Classifiers can exploit easy but misleading correlations instead of learning the intended visual or semantic signal. Many debiasing methods require explicit labels describing those correlations.
neurips-2020-learning-from-failure-de-bi.idea: Two networks learn together. One is deliberately encouraged to follow easy biases; the other emphasizes examples on which that biased network struggles, using its failures as a training signal.
neurips-2020-learning-from-failure-de-bi.results: Experiments across synthetic and real datasets improve performance under various biases, occasionally exceeding methods that receive explicit labels for spuriously correlated attributes.
neurips-2020-learning-from-failure-de-bi.limitations: The approach is motivated by biases being easier to learn than the desired signal, especially early in training. The abstract does not establish that all relevant biases meet that condition or provide numerical gains.
neurips-2020-learning-from-failure-de-bi.tldr: Use a deliberately biased model's failures to direct another model toward more reliable patterns.

neurips-2020-myersonian-regression-039e2.problem: Pricing creates an asymmetric prediction problem: charging too little loses some revenue, while charging above a buyer's value can lose the sale entirely. Ordinary squared-error regression does not capture this.
neurips-2020-myersonian-regression-039e2.idea: Myersonian regression fits a linear pricing function under a discontinuous revenue-based loss. The paper studies its computational difficulty and develops an additive approximation algorithm.
neurips-2020-myersonian-regression-039e2.results: Exact optimization is NP-hard, and a stronger efficient approximation scheme is excluded under the Exponential Time Hypothesis. A polynomial-time approximation scheme is provided, together with stability and generalization results.
neurips-2020-myersonian-regression-039e2.limitations: The algorithm's dependence on desired accuracy is exponential in a polynomial of inverse accuracy. Thus polynomial dependence on data size does not guarantee practicality at very high precision.
neurips-2020-myersonian-regression-039e2.tldr: Study linear price prediction using the actual asymmetric revenue consequences of overpricing and underpricing.

neurips-2021-a-realistic-approach-to-gen.problem: Face-recognition datasets collected before widespread mask wearing contain few masked faces. Models trained on them may struggle when much of a person's face is covered.
neurips-2021-a-realistic-approach-to-gen.idea: The authors overlay realistic synthetic masks using a face-filter development tool, with nine mask designs varying in color, shape, and fabric. They apply this process to CASIA-WebFace and CelebA.
neurips-2021-a-realistic-approach-to-gen.results: Volunteer comparisons favor the realism of the generated masks. FaceNet, VGG-face, and ArcFace trained on the enhanced datasets outperform equivalent models trained on original or competing synthetic-mask datasets when tested on masked faces.
neurips-2021-a-realistic-approach-to-gen.limitations: The training masks are synthetic, and the abstract does not give numerical recognition gains or detailed demographic and real-mask evaluation coverage.
neurips-2021-a-realistic-approach-to-gen.tldr: Augment existing face datasets with realistic synthetic masks to improve the tested masked-face recognition systems.

neurips-2021-adaptive-wavelet-distillati.problem: Accurate neural networks can be difficult to interpret and expensive to use. Scientific applications need compact representations whose predictive features can also be understood by domain experts.
neurips-2021-adaptive-wavelet-distillati.idea: Adaptive wavelet distillation learns a multiscale wavelet transform by penalizing a trained network's feature attributions in the wavelet domain. It transfers useful information into a concise representation.
neurips-2021-adaptive-wavelet-distillati.results: In cosmological parameter inference and molecular-partner prediction, the resulting models outperform compared neural networks and identify features judged scientifically meaningful through collaboration with domain experts.
neurips-2021-adaptive-wavelet-distillati.limitations: The abstract describes two application settings and does not quantify accuracy or efficiency gains. Interpretable features in these studies do not establish that every learned wavelet representation will have clear scientific meaning.
neurips-2021-adaptive-wavelet-distillati.tldr: Distill a neural network into a compact multiscale representation that supports both prediction and scientific interpretation.

neurips-2021-asynchronous-stochastic-opt.problem: Distributed training often applies gradients computed from outdated model parameters. A few unusually slow workers can make guarantees based on the maximum delay overly pessimistic.
neurips-2021-asynchronous-stochastic-opt.idea: The proposed stochastic optimizer tolerates arbitrary delays while its convergence bound depends on their average. This better reflects systems where most updates arrive promptly but occasional updates are very late.
neurips-2021-asynchronous-stochastic-opt.results: For smooth nonconvex objectives, the paper bounds the steps needed to reach approximate stationarity using gradient variance and average delay. Experiments show robustness under skewed and heavy-tailed delay distributions.
neurips-2021-asynchronous-stochastic-opt.limitations: The guarantee targets a stationary point rather than a global optimum. The abstract does not report wall-clock speedups or fully describe the algorithm's assumptions and implementation.
neurips-2021-asynchronous-stochastic-opt.tldr: Make asynchronous optimization guarantees depend on typical delay rather than the slowest observed update.

neurips-2021-csaw-m-an-ordinal-classific.problem: Breast tumors may be hidden by surrounding tissue in screening images. Image density is often used as a proxy, but it does not directly label the likelihood of this masking effect.
neurips-2021-csaw-m-an-ordinal-classific.idea: CSAW-M provides mammograms from more than 10,000 individuals with masking-potential assessments from five specialists. The authors train models to predict these ordered masking levels.
neurips-2021-csaw-m-an-ordinal-classific.results: Predicted masking is more informative about subsequent interval and large invasive cancers than the compared density estimates, even though the models were not explicitly trained to predict those cancer outcomes.
neurips-2021-csaw-m-an-ordinal-classific.limitations: The abstract does not provide effect sizes, clinical deployment results, or evidence that using the predictions improves patient outcomes. Predictive association and clinical benefit are different claims.
neurips-2021-csaw-m-an-ordinal-classific.tldr: Direct expert labels of mammographic masking support models more informative than density proxies in the reported evaluation.

neurips-2021-luna-linear-unified-nested-.problem: Standard attention compares many pairs of sequence positions, causing memory and computation to grow quadratically. This makes long sequences difficult to model efficiently.
neurips-2021-luna-linear-unified-nested-.idea: Luna first packs an input into a fixed-length auxiliary sequence, then unpacks information through a second attention operation. The nested construction approximates softmax attention with linear scaling in input length.
neurips-2021-luna-linear-unified-nested-.results: Evaluations on long-context tasks, machine translation, and masked language modeling show competitive or better results against full attention and several efficient attention alternatives.
neurips-2021-luna-linear-unified-nested-.limitations: The method approximates the original attention operation through a fixed-size intermediate representation. The abstract does not quantify which contexts lose information or give detailed accuracy-versus-compression tradeoffs.
neurips-2021-luna-linear-unified-nested-.tldr: Pass attention through a compact intermediate sequence to reduce the cost of processing long inputs.

neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.problem: Combining knowledge from separately trained Gaussian processes can require collecting their original datasets again. That adds computation and can conflict with keeping data decentralized.
neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.idea: The framework treats fitted Gaussian processes as reusable modules containing parameters, pseudo-inputs, and posterior distributions. A variational objective combines them into ensembles while transferring their learned uncertainty information.
neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.results: Experiments illustrate large-scale and multitask use, including comparison with exact inference methods. The framework also handles differing likelihoods and can learn correlations between previously independent output modules.
neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.limitations: The approach assumes a dictionary of well-fitted component models. The abstract does not quantify approximation errors or establish that avoiding data centralization itself provides a formal privacy guarantee.
neurips-2021-modular-gaussian-processes-.tldr: Reuse trained Gaussian-process modules and their uncertainty estimates without revisiting the original training data.

neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.problem: A standard privacy guarantee describes a worst case and may overstate an individual's actual privacy loss. Publishing a personalized estimate can itself reveal sensitive information about the underlying data.
neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.idea: The paper analyzes per-instance privacy for models trained using objective perturbation, which adds randomness to the learning objective. It then develops mechanisms for releasing the personalized privacy-loss estimates privately.
neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.results: The proposed methods are described as accurately publishing these losses with little or no additional privacy cost in the analyzed setting.
neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.limitations: The abstract does not give the precise privacy-accounting conditions, numerical accuracy, or scope of each release method. The claims concern objective perturbation rather than arbitrary private learning algorithms.
neurips-2021-privately-publishable-per-i.tldr: Provide more individualized privacy information while accounting for the privacy cost of revealing that information.

neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.problem: Binary neural networks use highly restricted values to reduce computation, but directly binarizing vision multilayer perceptrons can severely limit their ability to mix spatial and channel information.
neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.idea: BiMLP introduces multiple branches within binary blocks and shortcut connections between stages to enrich representations. Redesigned downsampling layers balance computation against classification quality.
neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.results: Experiments on ImageNet-1k show that the resulting models achieve higher accuracy than the prior binary convolutional networks compared in the paper.
neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.limitations: The abstract gives no numerical accuracy, speed, or memory measurements. Its main evidence comes from one image-classification benchmark, so benefits for other visual tasks or particular deployment hardware are not established here.
neurips-2022-bimlp-compact-binary-archit.tldr: Redesign binary vision MLP blocks to preserve more information while keeping the architecture compact.

neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.problem: Multimodal datasets often lack some measurements for particular examples. Learning one useful representation must accommodate both shared information and information unique to each modality.
neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.idea: CLUE extends multimodal variational autoencoders with cross-encoders that construct latent representations even when observations are incomplete. A semi-supervised framework connects information across the available modalities.
neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.results: On multimodal single-cell measurements, CLUE reports superior performance across all assessed categories of the NeurIPS 2021 single-cell data integration competition.
neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.limitations: The demonstrated application is single-cell genomics. The authors suggest broader uses, but the abstract does not present evaluations in other domains or specify numerical gains and sensitivity to different missing-data patterns.
neurips-2022-cross-linked-unified-embedd.tldr: Use cross-linked encoders to learn integrated representations from examples with missing measurement modalities.

neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.problem: Earth-system forecasts must model interactions across space and time. Physical simulations can be expensive, while applying attention directly to large observation arrays also creates computational challenges.
neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.idea: Earthformer divides spatiotemporal data into cuboids and performs attention within them in parallel. Global vectors connect these local computations so information can travel across the full system.
neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.results: Synthetic moving-image experiments guide the design. On real precipitation-nowcasting and El Niño/Southern Oscillation benchmarks, the model achieves the reported state-of-the-art performance.
neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.limitations: The abstract does not provide forecast skill values, uncertainty calibration, or evidence across all weather and climate regimes. Success on two benchmarks does not establish replacement of physical forecasting systems.
neurips-2022-earthformer-exploring-space.tldr: Combine local space-time attention with global connections to learn efficient Earth-system forecasts.

neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.problem: Attention can be slow and memory-intensive because it repeatedly transfers large intermediate arrays between GPU memory levels. Reducing arithmetic alone may not improve actual runtime.
neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.idea: FlashAttention computes exact attention in tiles arranged to reduce transfers between high-bandwidth memory and fast on-chip storage. The analysis explicitly accounts for this data movement.
neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.results: The abstract reports fewer memory accesses, threefold speedup for the stated GPT-2 setup, and 2.4-fold speedup on Long Range Arena. It also reports improved model evaluations and long-sequence capabilities.
neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.limitations: Exact attention still retains its underlying dense computation. Reported speedups belong to specific sequence lengths and experiments; the abstract does not establish the same gains on every hardware configuration.
neurips-2022-flashattention-fast-and-mem.tldr: Speed up exact attention by organizing computation around the GPU's memory hierarchy.

neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.problem: Forecasting world events requires using incomplete evidence available before outcomes are known. Language-model evaluations need realistic questions and careful protection against future-information leakage.
neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.idea: Autocast pairs thousands of tournament forecasting questions with a date-organized news corpus. IntervalQA separately tests numerical questions and calibration when answers span very different scales.
neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.results: Evaluated language models perform far below expert humans, but larger models and relevant retrieved news improve forecasts. The datasets establish a challenging benchmark for automated event prediction.
neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.limitations: The abstract reports no detailed forecast scores or evidence of expert-level performance. Historical evaluation with dated news also does not by itself establish reliability for future policy or economic decisions.
neurips-2022-forecasting-future-world-ev.tldr: Benchmark language-model forecasting with time-appropriate evidence and compare it directly with human expertise.

neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.problem: Robust control seeks policies that remain effective under disturbances. Directly optimizing such policies produces a constrained objective that is both nonconvex and nonsmooth, complicating convergence guarantees.
neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.idea: The paper analyzes the geometry of state-feedback H-infinity control. It shows that an appropriate notion of stationary point is globally optimal and that bounded-cost regions have useful compactness properties.
neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.results: These properties allow Goldstein-style subgradient methods and implementable variants to remain within stabilizing policies and eventually reach a global solution.
neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.limitations: The guarantee concerns the specified H-infinity state-feedback problem. The abstract does not provide convergence speeds, experimental comparisons, or analogous claims for arbitrary nonlinear control or reinforcement-learning tasks.
neurips-2022-global-convergence-of-direc.tldr: A difficult-looking robust-control objective has enough hidden structure to permit globally convergent direct policy search.

neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.problem: Scene graphs describe objects and their relationships, but recognizing one can depend on recognizing the other. Fixed prediction orderings may miss clues, especially for small or ambiguous objects.
neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.idea: The model repeatedly refines a scene graph using message passing and a transformer architecture. Each round conditions on the previous graph, allowing object and relationship predictions to inform one another.
neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.results: Experiments on Visual Genome and Action Genome show improved scene-graph generation. The framework can also improve the performance of existing approaches.
neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.limitations: The abstract does not quantify the gains, iteration count, or added inference cost. It establishes improvements on the named benchmarks without detailing which object or relationship categories benefit most.
neurips-2022-iterative-scene-graph-gener.tldr: Refine objects and relationships together over several rounds so each can help resolve ambiguity in the other.

neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.problem: Choosing the best option can require expensive simulations, but cheaper simulations provide biased approximations. Efficient experimentation must decide both what to test and how accurately to test it.
neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.idea: IISE progressively eliminates inferior options while choosing among simulation fidelities. Known bounds on approximation bias help determine when cheap evidence is sufficient and when accurate evaluation is needed.
neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.results: The paper derives a lower bound on identification cost and an algorithmic upper bound with similar structure. Simulated experiments demonstrate cost savings, with further theoretical improvements from more detailed bias knowledge.
neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.limitations: The analysis assumes known approximation-bias bounds. The abstract does not establish the same guarantees when these bounds are unknown or incorrect, and evaluations are simulated.
neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-best-arm-ide.tldr: Use cheap approximate simulations strategically while preserving confidence that the selected option is truly best.

neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.problem: Large image generators store extensive visual knowledge in their parameters, increasing model size and training demands. An external collection of examples may supply some of that information directly.
neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.idea: The approach conditions a smaller diffusion or autoregressive model on retrieved neighboring images. The database provides relevant content while the model learns how to compose it.
neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.results: Experiments report strong generation performance with fewer model parameters and demonstrate domain changes by swapping databases. Evaluations include class-conditional generation, stylization, and text-to-image tasks without paired text-image training data.
neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.limitations: The abstract does not give detailed parameter counts or retrieval costs. Generalization depends on the evaluated model-database combinations; replacing a database is not shown to solve every domain transfer.
neurips-2022-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.tldr: Let a smaller image generator consult retrieved examples instead of encoding all visual content in its weights.

neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.problem: Sometimes examples show which decisions worked for one task, but the underlying system is unknown and the new task differs. It is unclear whether those old decisions provide transferable guidance.
neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.idea: Social-Inverse formalizes learning one decision task from query-decision pairs belonging to another. The framework targets social-contagion management, where interactions and propagation can be complex and stochastic.
neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.results: A generalization analysis supports the learning framework. Experiments include a sanity check and comparisons with learning-based and graph-based alternatives, producing promising transfer results.
neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.limitations: The abstract does not specify task pairs, numerical improvements, or the conditions under which transfer fails. Its evidence concerns the social-contagion setting rather than arbitrary pairs of decision problems.
neurips-2022-social-inverse-inverse-deci.tldr: Learn useful decisions for a new contagion-management task from solutions to a related task.

neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.problem: Transporting material together along shared routes can reduce cost, favoring branching networks. Finding the best network must jointly solve where branches go and how they connect.
neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.idea: The paper separates geometric optimization for a fixed topology from combinatorial search over topologies. It studies structural restrictions on optimal branch points and combines both optimization components in an approximate solver.
neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.results: The authors give efficient geometry optimization for many sources and sinks, argue against optimal junctions with more than three incident edges, and extend results from the plane to two-dimensional curved spaces.
neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.limitations: The overall network problem remains NP-hard. The abstract does not give approximation ratios, runtime measurements, or claims for arbitrary higher-dimensional transport spaces.
neurips-2022-theory-and-approximate-solv.tldr: Exploit branching geometry and topology structure to approximate cost-efficient transport networks with multiple sources.

neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.problem: Encoding symmetries in a model can improve learning, but real data may follow a symmetry only approximately. Enforcing too much symmetry could prevent the model from fitting important exceptions.
neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.idea: The paper develops a quantitative framework relating a model's equivariance error to the corresponding error in the data distribution. Equivariance means predictions transform consistently when inputs undergo a specified transformation.
neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.results: The analysis provides generalization bounds for task-relevant symmetry and identifies conditions determining an optimal degree of approximate equivariance.
neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.limitations: The abstract describes theoretical results without experimental measurements. Its conclusions depend on the chosen symmetry group and the conditions in the bounds, rather than asserting that exact symmetry is always best.
neurips-2023-approximation-generalizatio.tldr: Balance the generalization benefit of symmetry against the need to represent departures from that symmetry.

neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.problem: AdaBoost emphasizes difficult examples through exponentially weighted updates. A more flexible weighting family could preserve fast learning while changing how strongly individual learners contribute.
neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.idea: The paper replaces ordinary exponential measures with tempered ones controlled by a parameter t. This yields t-AdaBoost, with standard AdaBoost as a special case, and related losses for decision trees.
neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.results: For the stated parameter range, the method retains exponential convergence and bounded learner coefficients. The derived losses satisfy strict properness, and experiments show benefits from tuning the temperature parameter.
neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.limitations: The abstract does not provide dataset-level gains or a universal rule for choosing t. The theoretical properties apply under the specified parameter ranges and learning assumptions.
neurips-2023-boosting-with-tempered-expo.tldr: Generalize boosting's exponential weighting with a tunable temperature while retaining strong convergence properties.

neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.problem: A three-dimensional detector trained on a limited category set must both locate unfamiliar objects and assign them new names. Neither localization nor classification can be assumed solved.
neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.idea: CoDA uses geometric cues and open-vocabulary image information to propose new 3D boxes. It then aligns point-cloud features with image and text features, iteratively improving discovery and classification together.
neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.results: Experiments on SUN-RGBD and ScanNet show substantial improvement over the best compared alternative; the abstract reports an 80% mAP improvement.
neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.limitations: The abstract does not provide absolute mAP values or the detailed evaluation protocol, so the reported percentage should not be read as an 80-point gain. Results concern the tested category and dataset settings.
neurips-2023-coda-collaborative-novel-bo.tldr: Discover unfamiliar 3D objects and align them with language jointly so each process improves the other.

neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.problem: Clustering usually makes discrete grouping decisions, which prevents ordinary backpropagation from adjusting earlier parts of an end-to-end learning system. Noisy data and unusual cluster shapes add difficulty.
neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.idea: The method builds clusters from minimum-weight spanning forests and introduces random perturbations to make useful gradients available. A dedicated loss also supports learning from partially specified clusters.
neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.results: The authors demonstrate supervised and semi-supervised applications on several datasets, reporting good performance even with high noise and challenging geometries.
neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.limitations: The abstract does not provide numerical comparisons, gradient-estimation costs, or the precise kinds of partial labels used. The stated robustness reflects the evaluated settings rather than a guarantee for all clustering structures.
neurips-2023-differentiable-clustering-w.tldr: Make graph-based clustering trainable inside a larger neural pipeline through stochastic perturbations.

neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.problem: Small fine-grained image datasets may cover only a narrow range of backgrounds, locations, or weather. Classifiers can then fail when the same category appears in a different context.
neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.idea: ALIA automatically describes dataset domains in language and uses those descriptions to guide image edits. A classifier filters out negligible edits and edits that damage class-relevant information.
neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.results: Experiments show improvements over traditional augmentation and text-to-image-generated training data on fine-grained classification, including domain-generalization and contextual-bias settings.
neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.limitations: The filtering step relies on a model trained on the original dataset, and the abstract does not quantify remaining labeling errors. Numerical gains, editing cost, and performance on untested domains are not specified.
neurips-2023-diversify-your-vision-datas.tldr: Create diverse but class-preserving image variations by combining automatic language descriptions, guided editing, and filtering.

neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.problem: Language models contain useful prior knowledge, but using them as standalone few-shot classifiers may not fully exploit it. Boosting offers a way to combine many modestly useful classifiers.
neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.idea: The method describes sampled tabular examples in text and asks a language model to produce a classification template. Repeating this under boosting's changing example distribution builds an ensemble of weak learners.
neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.results: The approach often outperforms tree-based boosting and few-shot prompting, and sometimes beats more involved fine-tuning, particularly with small datasets.
neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.limitations: The abstract demonstrates weak-learning behavior empirically for these tasks; it does not prove the full theoretical guarantee for every data distribution. Computational cost and detailed benchmark scores are absent.
neurips-2023-language-models-are-weak-le.tldr: Use prompted language models as components inside boosting rather than relying on one prompt-based classifier.

neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.problem: Offline imitation learning must learn from stored behavior without further environment interaction. When expert demonstrations are scarce and other trajectories are poor, copying the data can reproduce mistakes.
neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.idea: OILCA uses an identifiable variational autoencoder to construct counterfactual examples that augment expert data. The goal is to expand useful demonstrations and improve transfer across environmental changes.
neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.results: The paper analyzes the effect of generated data and reports improvements over baselines on DeepMind Control Suite for in-distribution behavior and CausalWorld for out-of-distribution generalization.
neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.limitations: The abstract does not specify the identifiability assumptions or quantify counterfactual validity. Results on the named benchmarks do not establish that generated demonstrations remain useful in every offline robotics setting.
neurips-2023-offline-imitation-learning-.tldr: Augment scarce expert demonstrations with modeled counterfactuals to improve offline imitation and environmental generalization.

neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.problem: Constrained nonconvex optimization can require complex nested procedures, especially when objectives or constraints have sharp corners. Simpler switching subgradient methods lacked comparable nonconvex complexity guarantees.
neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.idea: The method switches between objective improvement and constraint handling within one loop. The paper analyzes it for weakly convex objectives with either convex or weakly convex constraint functions.
neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.results: The analysis establishes oracle complexity for reaching a nearly stationary point, matching the compared nested approaches while accommodating nonsmooth functions and avoiding inner-loop iteration tuning.
neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.limitations: The guarantee concerns near-stationarity under the specified weak-convexity assumptions, not a global solution. The abstract does not provide numerical experiments or wall-clock comparisons demonstrating the practical savings.
neurips-2023-oracle-complexity-of-single.tldr: A simple single-loop method gains convergence guarantees for an important class of nonsmooth constrained problems.

neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.problem: Protecting feature vectors with differential privacy can reduce their usefulness for search or classification. Random-projection methods need noise mechanisms that preserve more task-relevant information.
neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.idea: The paper improves private random projections and designs private sign projections around how likely a small input change is to flip a projected sign. Smooth flipping probabilities guide more useful randomization.
neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.results: Retrieval and classification experiments favor the proposed methods over standard randomized-response approaches, with DP-SignOPORP generally strongest among the evaluated private projection methods.
neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.limitations: The abstract does not state privacy budgets, numerical accuracy losses, or all assumptions behind the guarantees. Its expectation of broader industrial adoption is a motivation, not an evaluated result.
neurips-2023-smooth-flipping-probability.tldr: Exploit the stability of projected signs to improve the utility of differentially private data representations.

neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.problem: Transformer layers produce many possible representations, but the final layer may not be the most useful for a downstream task. Researchers need a way to identify informative layers without labels.
neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.idea: The study tracks intrinsic dimension and neighborhood composition across layers. These geometric measurements describe how representations expand, compress, and organize examples during processing.
neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.results: Across the studied protein and image models, dimensions rise early and contract in intermediate layers. The authors propose choosing intermediate representations near a relative dimension minimum to capture useful semantic information.
neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.limitations: The abstract reports recurring empirical patterns rather than a universal theorem for all transformers. It does not quantify downstream improvements or fully specify when the proposed layer-selection rule fails.
neurips-2023-the-geometry-of-hidden-repr.tldr: Use representation geometry to locate intermediate transformer layers that may be especially useful for downstream learning.

neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.problem: Text prompts alone offer limited control over the precise layout or geometry of generated images. Supporting many kinds of visual guidance in one model adds another challenge.
neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.idea: UniControl extends a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model with a task-aware hypernetwork. Visual conditions guide structure while language guides context and style across multiple condition-to-image tasks.
neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.results: After training on nine tasks, the model demonstrates generation from unseen visual conditions and often surpasses similarly sized single-task control models in the reported experiments.
neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.limitations: The abstract does not quantify control precision, success rates, or the range of unseen conditions tested. The word 'often' also indicates that improvement over specialized models is not universal.
neurips-2023-unicontrol-a-unified-diffus.tldr: Combine several visual-control tasks in one diffusion model while preserving natural-language guidance.

neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.problem: A graph classifier may behave differently when graphs become much larger than those seen during development. Understanding this limiting behavior reveals constraints on size generalization.
neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.idea: The paper studies classifiers on increasingly large graphs drawn from the Erdős–Rényi random-graph model. Under stated mild assumptions, it analyzes whether a particular output remains likely.
neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.results: For the covered class of graph neural networks, including graph convolutional networks, output probabilities converge to zero or one. Experiments observe the predicted tendency even on relatively small graphs.
neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.limitations: The result depends on the specified random-graph distribution, architecture class, and assumptions. It does not claim that every GNN becomes constant on every family of large real-world graphs.
neurips-2023-zero-one-laws-of-graph-neur.tldr: Certain graph networks have sharply restricted asymptotic behavior on growing random graphs.

neurips-2024-4m-21-an-any-to-any-vision-.problem: Unified vision models can perform only the kinds of tasks represented during training. Expanding to many different input and output formats requires a common representation that preserves their useful structure.
neurips-2024-4m-21-an-any-to-any-vision-.idea: 4M-21 converts images, text, geometry, model features, poses, and other modalities into discrete tokens. Joint training combines multimodal datasets and text, including information distilled from specialist models.
neurips-2024-4m-21-an-any-to-any-vision-.results: The authors report at least three times as many tasks or modalities as existing models without performance loss, finer generation control, and scaling to three billion parameters.
neurips-2024-4m-21-an-any-to-any-vision-.limitations: The abstract does not give per-task scores or establish competence for arbitrary untrained modalities. Its broad coverage still depends on the tokenization choices and training sources supplied to the model.
